_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. The seven silhouettes are an I-section beam, a box module with openings, a tracked machine with an articulated arm, a box with a big round grille, a cone-bottomed cylinder on legs, a bundle of rolled sheets, and an open braced frame. Classes II and IV are both boxes, so the module gets door and window openings and corner lugs while the plant unit gets a circular fan grille and a squatter proportion. Class V avoids timber and steel, both of which are entries in class I, and uses a cement silo instead; class VI avoids a tripod-mounted scanner, since reality capture is also an entry in class III, and uses drawings. The palette override has to forbid yellow and orange by name — earthmoving equipment and site safety gear are those colors in life.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including painted machinery, timber, brick, concrete and safety markings, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow, green or wood brown anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A single short length of wide-flange structural steel beam standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: two parallel flat flanges joined by a single central web so the top face reads clearly as a capital I, with a row of four round bolt holes punched through the web and a plain flat end plate welded across the top. Heavy, blunt and geometric, the I-shaped section the whole point. One piece alone: no building, no connections, no other members, no bolts fitted.
partPrompts.2: A single volumetric building module sitting on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a plain rectangular box roughly twice as long as it is wide and about one story tall, with one door-sized opening in a long side and one window-sized opening beside it, both empty, a flat roof, and one small square lifting lug standing up at each top corner. Blank walls otherwise. One module alone, no crane, no chains, no truck, no site, no interior visible.
partPrompts.3: A single compact tracked excavator standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a low rectangular body on two long tracks, with a boom rising from the front of the body, folding once at an elbow, and ending in a plain toothed bucket resting on the ground ahead of the machine. Tracks plus one folded arm, the whole thing squat and heavy. No spoil heap, no trench, no dirt, no operator, no other machines, no markings.
partPrompts.4: A single outdoor heat pump unit standing on a low plain base, seen three-quarter: a rectangular sheet-metal case clearly wider than it is tall, with one large circular fan grille of a few concentric rings set in the middle of the front face, a panel of closely spaced vertical coil fins along one whole side, and two short pipe stubs leaving the opposite side. Squat and wide, the round grille the identifying feature. One unit alone, no wall, no house, no ducting, no wiring.
partPrompts.5: A single bulk cement silo standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tall smooth vertical cylinder closing into a steep cone at the bottom, carried about a third of the way up by four straight splayed legs so the cone hangs clear of the ground, with a short outlet spout at the tip of the cone, a small flat cap on top, and a straight vertical ladder running up one side. Tall, round and cone-bottomed. One silo alone: no truck, no plant, no hoses, no dust, no markings.
partPrompts.6: A bundle of rolled drawing sheets lying on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: three tightly rolled tubes of paper of slightly different lengths lying together, the loose spiral edge of the paper visible at the near ends, a plain flat band around the middle holding them together, and one sheet unrolled just enough at the far end to show a soft curl. Completely blank paper. Three rolls and nothing else: no printing, no lines, no drawings visible, no desk, no tools.
partPrompts.7: A single bay of tubular scaffolding standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: an open frame of straight round tubes, two upright standards on each side joined by horizontal rails at two heights and one long diagonal brace across the near face, with a flat plank deck laid across the frame near the top and a plain base plate under each standard. Open and skeletal, so the background shows through it. One bay only: no building behind it, no ladders, no netting, no workers, no tools.
